mainTopic: What the יום הכיפורים and other goat offerings atone for, how the כהנים are atoned for, and why מסכת שבועות follows מכות.
overview: This amud finishes the first משנה of שבועות, which explains what atones for each kind of sin. רבי מאיר says all the extra goat offerings atone for the same thing: טומאת מקדש וקדשיו. רבי שמעון gives each goat its own case, from ראש חודש through the רגלים to יום הכיפורים. The חכמים ask whether a goat set aside for one day may be brought on another. He says yes, because all of them come to atone for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו. רבי שמעון בן יהודה reports a second version of רבי שמעון's view, in which each set of goats covers more cases than the one before. The same question and answer then repeat for that version. The משנה then rules that deliberate טומאת מקדש וקדשיו is atoned for by the inside goat and the day of יום הכיפורים, and that the שעיר המשתלח atones for all other sins. The תנא קמא and רבי שמעון disagree about how far the כהן גדול's פר does for the כהנים what the goats do for Israel. Finally the גמרא opens by asking why שבועות follows מכות, and begins an answer that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: What the ראש חודש goats atone for
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes רבי שמעון's earlier answer: the goats of ראש חודש atone for a טהור person who ate טמא sacrificial food.
steps.simpleTranslation: They atone for a pure person who ate impure food.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is finishing a sentence that began just before this. It answers the question of what the ראש חודש goats atone for, according to רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון had just said that the ראש חודש goats do not atone for the case where a person was never aware of the impurity. So the משנה asked what they do atone for. The answer is a narrow case: the person was טהור, but the קדשים food he ate had become טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who is ritually pure
Who ate
Ritually impure (here: sacrificial food that became impure)

steps.confusionAlert: Here the person is pure and the food is impure. It is not an impure person eating pure food.

phrases.english: For a pure person who ate impure food.
phrases.notes: This answers the question just before this line: what do the ראש חודש goats atone for? The food here is קדשים that became טמא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבי שמעון's answer from the earlier part of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What do the ראש חודש goats atone for, according to רבי שמעון?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: For a טהור person who unknowingly ate טמא קדשים.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: all the goats atone for the same thing
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר holds that every goat offering atones for the same sin: טומאת מקדש וקדשיו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: all the goats have the same atonement. They atone for impurity of the מקדש and its sacred foods.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר gives his own view. He does not split up the goats. To him they all do the same job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier opinions in the משנה gave each goat its own case to cover. רבי מאיר disagrees with that whole approach. For him the goats of ראש חודש, the רגלים and יום הכיפורים all atone equally for each of the unwitting cases of טומאת מקדש וקדשיו that the other opinions divide among them.

keyTerms.meaning: Goats brought as extra (מוסף) sin offerings
Their atonement
The same, equal
Entering the מקדש while impure, or eating its sacred foods while impure

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:
All the goats, their atonement is the same,
for impurity of the Temple and its sacred foods.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the opinions that give each goat a separate job.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All the goat offerings atone the same way, for each of the unwitting cases of טומאת מקדש וקדשיו that the other opinions divide among them.

steps.title: רבי שמעון lists the job of each goat
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון explains his full view: the ראש חודש goats cover a טהור person who ate טמא food. The רגלים goats cover a case with no ידיעה at all. The יום הכיפורים goats cover a case with ידיעה only at the end.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון used to say: the ראש חודש goats atone for a pure person who ate impure food. The goats of the רגלים atone where there was no awareness, not at the beginning and not at the end. The goat of יום הכיפורים atones where there was no awareness at the beginning but there was awareness at the end.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lays out רבי שמעון's whole system in one place. This sets up the conversation with the חכמים that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike רבי מאיר, רבי שמעון gives each goat its own separate case. The cases differ by when the person knew about the impurity: before the sin, after it, or never. This split is exactly what the חכמים will question next.

keyTerms.meaning: The first days of the months (ראש חודש)
The pilgrimage festivals
Awareness, knowing about the impurity
At the beginning, before the sin
At the end, after the sin
יום כיפור

steps.confusionAlert: ידיעה here means knowing that you were impure, or that the place or food was holy. 'Beginning' means before the sin and 'end' means after it. It is not talking about the start or end of the day.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon would say:
The goats of the New Moons atone
for a pure person who ate impure food,
and those of the Festivals atone
for a case where there is no awareness,
not at the beginning and not at the end,
and that of Yom Kippur atones
for a case where there is no awareness at the beginning
but there is awareness at the end.
phrases.notes: This is the יום הכיפורים מוסף goat, not the special goat of the day's עבודה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets רבי שמעון's divided system against רבי מאיר's single one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each goat atones for a different case: ראש חודש for a טהור person who ate טמא food, רגלים for no ידיעה at all, and יום הכיפורים for ידיעה only at the end.

steps.title: Can one goat be brought in place of another?
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ask רבי שמעון whether a goat set aside for one day may be offered on a different day.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: what is the law, may they be offered one in place of the other?
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים ask רבי שמעון a practical question. It sets up the challenge that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether a goat set aside for one occasion, like יום הכיפורים, can be used for another, like a רגל. Since רבי שמעון gives each goat a different job, the question tests his system.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the law?
That they be offered
This one in place of that one

phrases.english: They said to him:
phrases.notes: 'They' are the חכמים, speaking to רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: What is the law, may they be offered one in place of the other?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: מַהוּ שֶׁיִּקְרְבוּ זֶה בָּזֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how רבי שמעון's system works in practice.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: May a goat set aside for one day's offering be brought on a different day?

steps.title: רבי שמעון: yes, they may be swapped
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון answers that the goats may be offered one in place of the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: they may be offered.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון gives a short, direct answer: yes, you may switch them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His answer is surprising, since he just said each goat has its own case. That tension sets up the חכמים's challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: He said to them
They may be offered

phrases.english: He said to them: They may be offered.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, a goat for one day may be offered on another day.

steps.title: How can they be swapped if they atone differently?
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים challenge רבי שמעון: if each goat atones for something different, how can one replace another?
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: since their atonement is not the same, how can they be offered one in place of the other?
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים point out a contradiction in רבי שמעון's position. They are attacking his answer from step 5.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their logic: a goat meant to atone for case A should not be able to atone for case B. So if the jobs differ, swapping should not work. This seems to clash with his own list in step 3.

keyTerms.meaning: Since
How?
Are offered

phrases.english: They said to him:
Since their atonement is not the same,
how can they be offered one in place of the other?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: הוֹאִיל וְאֵין כַּפָּרָתָן שָׁוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי שמעון's answer in step 5 using his own view from step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's ruling that the goats may be swapped.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If each goat covers a different case, a goat set aside for one case cannot do the job of another, so swapping should not be allowed.

steps.title: All the goats share one category
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון answers that all the goats come to atone for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו, so they can be swapped.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: all of them come to atone for impurity of the מקדש and its sacred foods.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון defends himself. The goats share one big category, so one can stand in for another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He separates the general category from the specific case each goat covers. All the goats belong to the category of טומאת מקדש וקדשיו. The different cases are only how that atonement is divided up, so the goats are still the same kind of offering and can be exchanged.

keyTerms.meaning: All of them
Come to atone

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: all the goats atone for the same thing. רבי שמעון: each goat covers a different case, but all within the one category of טומאת מקדש וקדשיו. That is why, even for him, they may be swapped.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a basic idea that comes up often: things can have different specific jobs yet still count as one category in הלכה.

phrases.english: He said to them:
All of them come to atone
for impurity of the Temple and its sacred foods.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Separating the general category from the specific case each goat covers.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A different specific case means the goats are completely different offerings and cannot be swapped.
steps.terutzMaskana: They all share the category of טומאת מקדש וקדשיו, so one may be offered in place of another.

steps.title: A second version of רבי שמעון's view, where each set of goats adds on to the one before
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן יהודה reports רבי שמעון's view differently. The ראש חודש goats cover a טהור person who ate טמא food. The רגלים goats cover that case plus a case with no ידיעה at all. The יום הכיפורים goats cover both of those plus a case with ידיעה only at the end.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן יהודה says in רבי שמעון's name: the ראש חודש goats atone for a pure person who ate impure sacred food. The רגלים goats go further. They atone for that case and also for a case where the person never knew, not at the beginning and not at the end. The יום הכיפורים goats go further still. They atone for both of those cases and also for a case where the person did not know at the beginning but found out at the end.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a second report of רבי שמעון's opinion. In this report each set of goats covers everything the earlier set covers, plus one more case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version (Step 3), each set of goats had its own separate job. Here the jobs stack up. Each set includes the earlier cases and adds a new one, so the יום הכיפורים goats cover all three cases. This stacking matters for the next question, because it means the goats are no longer equal to each other.

keyTerms.meaning: In his name, meaning in רבי שמעון's name
Adds on top of them. These goats cover more than the earlier ones
The goat offerings brought on ראש חודש
The festivals: פסח, שבועות and סוכות

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new opinion from a different תנא. רבי שמעון בן יהודה is only reporting רבי שמעון's own view in a different form.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשְּׁמוֹ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda says in his name:
phrases.notes: "His name" means רבי שמעון, whose view the משנה just gave.

phrases.english: The goats of the New Moons

phrases.aramaic: מְכַפְּרִין עַל הַטָּהוֹר שֶׁאָכַל אֶת הַטָּמֵא.
phrases.english: atone for a pure person who ate impure food.
phrases.notes: He means impure sacred food, eaten without realizing it.

phrases.english: Those of the Festivals go beyond them,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁמְּכַפְּרִין עַל טָהוֹר שֶׁאָכַל אֶת הַטָּמֵא,
phrases.english: for they atone for a pure person who ate impure food,
and for a case that has no awareness,
neither at the beginning nor at the end.
Those of Yom Kippur go beyond them,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהֵן מְכַפְּרִין עַל הַטָּהוֹר שֶׁאָכַל אֶת הַטָּמֵא,
phrases.english: for they atone for a pure person who ate impure food,
and for a case that has no awareness,
neither at the beginning nor at the end,
and for a case that has no awareness at the beginning
but does have awareness at the end.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשְּׁמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of the view from Step 3, now built in stacked layers instead of separate jobs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each set of goats covers all the cases of the set before it plus one more: ראש חודש covers one case, רגלים cover two, and יום הכיפורים covers three.

steps.title: The חכמים ask whether goats from different days can replace each other
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ask רבי שמעון, according to this stacked version, whether a goat set aside for one day may be offered on another day.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: may these goats be offered one in place of the other?
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים ask a practical question about this second version: can the goats be swapped between days? This sets up the next exchange.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words match the question in Step 4, but now it is asked about the stacked version. Because the goats now cover different amounts, the question is sharper than before.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the law? Used to open a question
That they be offered
This one in place of that one

phrases.english: They said to him:
What is the law, may they be offered this one in place of that one?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: מַהוּ שֶׁיִּקְרְבוּ זֶה בָּזֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks a practical question about the stacked version just given.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a goat set aside for one day may be offered on a different day under the stacked version.

steps.title: רבי שמעון answers yes
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון answers that yes, the goats may be offered in place of one another.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון gives a short answer: yes, the goats can be swapped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He allows swapping in every direction. That opens the door for the חכמים to point out a problem, because the goats in this version do not cover the same things.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes

phrases.english: He said to them: Yes.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, the goats may be swapped between days.

steps.title: Swapping makes sense in only one direction
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים argue that a יום הכיפורים goat can be used on ראש חודש, since it covers more. But a ראש חודש goat cannot do the job on יום הכיפורים, because it would have to atone for cases it was never set aside for.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: if so, fine, the יום הכיפורים goats can be offered on ראש חודש. But how can the ראש חודש goats be offered on יום הכיפורים, to bring an atonement that is not theirs?
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים challenge רבי שמעון's yes. They say it works only one way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the stacked version, a יום הכיפורים goat already covers the ראש חודש case, so using it on ראש חודש is no problem. A ראש חודש goat covers only one case. On יום הכיפורים it would have to cover two extra cases it was never meant for. This is different from Step 6, where the problem was that each goat had a separate job. Here the problem runs in one direction only.

keyTerms.meaning: If so. Accepting a claim in order to show a problem with it
How? Here it is a challenge
An atonement that is not its own, one it was not set aside for

phrases.english: They said to him: If so,

phrases.aramaic: יִהְיוּ שֶׁל יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים קְרֵבִין בְּרָאשֵׁי חֳדָשִׁים;
phrases.english: fine, those of Yom Kippur can be offered on the New Moons;
but how can those of the New Moons
be offered on Yom Kippur,
to bring an atonement that is not theirs?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the yes given in Step 10, based on the stacked structure of Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's ruling that the goats may be swapped in every direction.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A goat that covers less, the ראש חודש goat, cannot fill in for one that covers more, the יום הכיפורים goat, because it would be atoning for cases it was never set aside for.

steps.title: All the goats share one purpose: טומאת מקדש וקדשיו
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון answers that all the goats come to atone for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו, so any of them can be offered on any of the days.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: all of them come to atone for making the מקדש or its sacred foods impure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון answers the challenge. All the goats belong to one shared category, so swapping is allowed in both directions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each goat is set aside for the general sin of טומאת מקדש וקדשיו, not for one specific case. Which case a goat ends up covering depends on the day it is offered, not on why it was set aside. So a ראש חודש goat offered on יום הכיפורים simply does what a יום הכיפורים goat does.

keyTerms.meaning: All of them
Come to atone
Making the מקדש or its sacred foods impure

steps.whatToRemember: In both versions of רבי שמעון's view, the goats can be swapped. Each covers different cases, but all of them share one purpose: atoning for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו.

phrases.english: He said to them:
All of them come to atone
for impurity of the Temple and its sacred foods.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם: כּוּלָּן בָּאִין לְכַפֵּר עַל טוּמְאַת מִקְדָּשׁ וְקָדָשָׁיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the one-direction challenge of Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a shared overall category that the specific cases fall under
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each goat is tied to the specific cases of its own day, so a ראש חודש goat cannot cover the extra יום הכיפורים cases.
steps.terutzMaskana: All the goats are set aside for the general sin of טומאת מקדש וקדשיו, so each one atones for whatever that day covers.

steps.title: What atones for deliberate טומאת מקדש וקדשיו
steps.stepSummary: The משנה returns to its main list and rules that deliberate טומאת מקדש וקדשיו is atoned for by the inside goat of יום הכיפורים together with the day of יום הכיפורים itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for deliberately making the מקדש or its sacred foods impure, the goat whose service is done inside and the day of יום הכיפורים atone.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה leaves רבי שמעון's view and goes back to its main list of what atones for what. Now it covers someone who made the מקדש or its sacred foods impure on purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everything before this dealt with doing it without knowing. For doing it on purpose, two things work together: the goat whose blood is brought inside on יום הכיפורים, and the day of יום הכיפורים itself.

keyTerms.meaning: On purpose, deliberately
The goat whose service is done inside, the יום הכיפורים goat whose blood is brought inside
The day of יום הכיפורים itself also atones

phrases.english: And for deliberate impurity of the Temple and its sacred foods,
the goat whose service is done inside
phrases.notes: This is the יום הכיפורים goat whose blood is brought inside the Sanctuary.

phrases.english: and Yom Kippur atone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion of רבי שמעון's view and returns to the משנה's main list of what atones for each kind of טומאת מקדש וקדשיו.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Deliberate טומאת מקדש וקדשיו is atoned for by the inside goat of יום הכיפורים together with the day of יום הכיפורים itself.

steps.title: The scapegoat atones for all other sins
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that every other sin in the Torah, of any type or severity, is atoned for by the שעיר המשתלח.
steps.simpleTranslation: For all the other sins in the Torah, whether light or severe, on purpose or by accident, known or not known, positive commands or prohibitions, punished by כרת or by a court execution, the שעיר המשתלח atones.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its list of what atones for what. Everything not connected to טומאת מקדש וקדשיו is atoned for by the שעיר המשתלח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the משנה dealt only with sins of טומאת מקדש וקדשיו. Now it covers all the other sins in one sweep. It lists pairs of opposites to show that no kind of sin is left out.

keyTerms.meaning: All the other sins, meaning the ones not about טומאת מקדש וקדשיו
Light sins and severe sins
Sins done on purpose and sins done by accident
Sins punished by כָּרֵת, being cut off by Heaven
Sins punished by a court-imposed death penalty
The goat sent away to עֲזָאזֵל on יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה splits atonement into two areas. Sins of טומאת מקדש וקדשיו are handled separately: in the cases this משנה lists, the goats whose blood is offered atone (and for the כהנים, the פר, as the next step says). Every other sin goes to the שעיר המשתלח.

phrases.english: For the other sins in the Torah:
the light ones and the severe ones,
the deliberate ones and the accidental ones,
whether he became aware or did not become aware,
positive commands and prohibitions,
those punished by כרת and those punished by court executions –
the goat that is sent away atones.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list after the ruling on deliberate טומאת מקדש וקדשיו, and moves on to all other sins.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every other sin in the Torah, of any type, is atoned for by the שעיר המשתלח.

steps.title: Israelites and priests share the same atonement
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא rules that Israelites, כהנים and the כהן משוח are atoned for equally. The only difference is that the פר atones for the כהנים for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Israelites, כהנים and the כהן משוח are all the same. What is the difference between them? Only that the פר atones for the כהנים for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה says everyone, including the כהנים and the כהן גדול, gets atonement from the שעיר המשתלח for other sins. It points out just one difference between the groups.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For ordinary sins there is no difference at all: the שעיר המשתלח covers everyone. The one exception is טומאת מקדש וקדשיו. For that, the כהנים are covered by the כהן גדול's פר and not by the goats.

keyTerms.meaning: The anointed priest, meaning the כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל
What is the difference between
The bull the כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל brings on יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים

phrases.english: Both Israelites and priests
and the anointed priest are all the same.
phrases.notes: The משנה is still talking about the שעיר המשתלח: it atones for all three groups alike.

phrases.english: What is the difference between Israelites
and priests and the anointed priest?
Only that the bull atones for the priests –
for impurity of the Temple and its holy foods.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶחָד יִשְׂרְאֵלִים וְאֶחָד כֹּהֲנִים וְאֶחָד כֹּהֵן מָשׁוּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out who is covered by the שעיר המשתלח from step 14, and notes one difference.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שעיר המשתלח atones equally for Israelites, כהנים and the כהן משוח. Only for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו are the כהנים atoned for by the פר.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: the bull does for priests what the goats do for Israel
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון makes a full parallel. The פר's blood atones for the כהנים like the inside goat's blood does for Israel. The פר's וידוי atones for the כהנים like the שעיר המשתלח's וידוי does for Israel.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: Just as the blood of the goat brought inside atones for Israel, so the blood of the פר atones for the כהנים. Just as the confession over the שעיר המשתלח atones for Israel, so the confession over the פר atones for the כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון disagrees with the תנא קמא about how the כהנים get atonement. He sets up two matching pairs between the goats for Israel and the פר for the כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא said the פר helps the כהנים only for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו. רבי שמעון adds a second job for the פר: its וידוי covers the כהנים' other sins, just as the שעיר המשתלח's וידוי covers Israel. So for רבי שמעון, the פר is the כהנים' full match for both Israelite goats.

keyTerms.meaning: Just as... so too, a way of drawing a parallel
Done inside, meaning the goat whose blood is brought into the היכל and קֹדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים
Confession said over the animal

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read רבי שמעון as merely agreeing with the תנא קמא. His second parallel is the new point: for the כהנים' other sins, the פר's וידוי does the job that the שעיר המשתלח does for Israel.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
Just as the blood of the goat
that is offered inside atones for Israel,

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ דַּם הַפָּר מְכַפֵּר עַל הַכֹּהֲנִים;
phrases.english: so the blood of the bull atones for the priests;
just as the confession over the goat that is sent away
atones for Israel,

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ וִידּוּיוֹ שֶׁל פָּר מְכַפֵּר עַל הַכֹּהֲנִים.
phrases.english: so the confession over the bull atones for the priests.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁדַּם הַשָּׂעִיר הַנַּעֲשֶׂה בִּפְנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different view from the תנא קמא in step 15 about how the כהנים are atoned for.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For the כהנים, the פר's blood matches the inside goat's blood, and the פר's וידוי matches the שעיר המשתלח's וידוי.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה ends in a dispute. The תנא קמא says the כהנים share the שעיר המשתלח with everyone else. רבי שמעון says the כהנים' פר matches both Israelite goats.

steps.title: Why does שבועות come right after מכות?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking why the תנא follows מסכת מכות with מסכת שבועות.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The תנא is just finishing מכות. Why does he teach שבועות next?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its discussion of the perek. It asks what connects the end of מכות to the start of שבועות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes the order of the מסכתות is not random. It wants a link between the last topic of מכות and the opening topic of שבועות.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the מִשְׁנָה
Now, since; an opener that sets up a question
The teacher of the מִשְׁנָה
Is coming up from, meaning just finishing

phrases.english: Gemara
Now, the teacher of the משנה is just finishing מכות;
phrases.notes: מכות is the מסכת printed right before שבועות.

phrases.english: why is it that he teaches שבועות next?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּדֵי תַּנָּא מִמַּכּוֹת סָלֵיק, מַאי שְׁנָא דְּתָנֵי שְׁבוּעוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The משנה is finished, and the גמרא starts its own discussion with a question about the order of the מסכתות.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What links the end of מכות to the start of שבועות, explaining why שבועות comes next.

steps.title: The link begins: 'liable for two on the head'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts its answer by quoting the end of מכות: one is liable for two sets of lashes on the head, one for each side.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the תנא taught there: one is liable for two on the head, one from this side and one from that side.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins answering by quoting the last משנה of מכות. The answer continues on the next amud, where the גמרא finishes connecting this 'two' to שבועות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The quoted line uses the pattern of 'two' that come out of one area: rounding the head counts as two violations, one for each side. This sets up the link to the opening of שבועות, which also begins by counting things in twos.

keyTerms.meaning: Because he taught
Liable for two punishments

phrases.english: Because he taught:
phrases.notes: He is quoting the last משנה in מכות, about rounding the edges of the head.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The link comes from the end of מכות, which teaches 'liable for two' on the head. The full connection to שבועות is completed on the next amud.
